# @spellkave/behaviour

> `behaviour-docs` — Black-box behaviour suites that document a package: the run becomes a guide and evidence, the package's own sources become its README.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `behaviour-docs readme [<package dir>] [--scope <suite>]` | Write the package's README.md, offline, from its docs config, features, header comments, unit-test markers and scripts. |
| `behaviour-docs report [<package dir>] [--scope <suite>] [--open]` | Render the last behaviour run as an Allure 3 HTML report in behaviour/<scope>/.report (local, not committed); --open serves it. |
| `behaviour-docs guide [<package dir>] [--scope <suite>]` | Write docs/guide.md and docs/scenarios.md from the last behaviour run in behaviour/.results. |

## What it promises

No behaviour scenarios yet: the package is tested by its unit tests and by the suites that use it.

## Design

Each part's header comment, as written next to the code.

### [`src/cli.ts`](src/cli.ts)

Runs a real command-line tool as a black box: argv in, stdout/stderr/exit
code out. Nothing of the tool is imported. Every run a step attaches becomes
a transcript in the results, with machine paths replaced so it can be
published.

### [`src/endpoint.ts`](src/endpoint.ts)

A child owns its listening socket from bind until stop. Read its bound port
from a complete readiness line; never reserve a port and release it before
starting the real listener. Logs remain available after readiness and failure.

### [`src/narrate.ts`](src/narrate.ts)

Domain-free glue between Gherkin (QuickPickle) and Allure: tags become
labels, and every step shows up as an Allure step named after its Gherkin
sentence, prefixed with its keyword. Gherkin data tables are attached to
their step.

Tags: @persona:<slug> -> epic; Feature -> feature (the goal); Scenario ->
story; a scenario inside `Rule:` -> layer=rule + rule=<text>, otherwise
layer=intent; @code:<path>:<symbol> -> label code (the guide links it);
@planned -> skipped, labels kept.

### [`src/contract-steps.ts`](src/contract-steps.ts)

Steps every JSONL command-line tool shares: how it answers, not what it
does. A package registers them once, naming its tool, next to its own steps.

### [`src/vitest.ts`](src/vitest.ts)

The Vitest configuration of a behaviour suite: Gherkin files run through
QuickPickle, results go to Allure's result format (read by the guide
generator and by `behaviour-docs report`). Every run starts by clearing the
suite's results (global-setup.ts), so no older run leaks into the documents.
Feature files run one after another unless the suite says its scenarios
share nothing.

### [`src/setup.ts`](src/setup.ts)

The start of a behaviour run, called from a package's Vitest globalSetup:
one run, one result set, so the documents are generated from exactly this
run. It records the commit the run tests (not the commit the documents are
later generated at) and whether the code it depends on had local changes.
A suite whose tool starts through tsx also bundles it here, once per run.

### [`src/global-setup.ts`](src/global-setup.ts)

The Vitest globalSetup every behaviour suite runs first (behaviourConfig
adds it): one run, one result set. It clears the suite's results directory,
so the guide and the Allure report never mix in an older run, and records
the commit the run tests. A package's own globalSetup may still call
`startRun` with a wider set of watched paths; that overwrites run.json.

### [`src/world.ts`](src/world.ts)

A world for one behaviour scenario (D-6 in
ledger/designs/behaviour-first-tests.md). Scenarios never start nodes; they
get a world source and read the world only through
`{url}/v1/database/{db}/sql` with `token`. `url`, `db` and `token` may change
after `reset`, so read them after every `await reset(...)`.

- "wiped": the module is published, nothing is seeded.
- "seeded": the module plus the standard seed manifest.

### [`src/world-pooled.ts`](src/world-pooled.ts)

Pooled world source: each `reset` leases a fresh database from the shared
SpacetimeDB test host (stdb pool, sk-jay0.7.209) instead of restoring a
local node, so scenarios get their own `db` and can run in parallel.

`reset` never clears or deletes. SpacetimeDB 2.10.x exits the whole shared
host when a database is deleted or clear-published while a client still
calls it, so the pool server refuses DELETE, clear and publish for tenants,
and a used database is only abandoned (released, never touched again). The
host is recycled from a golden data dir when it runs out of headroom.

`await reset(baseline)` returns only when the leased database answers SQL
with the lease token: the pool touches it before answering, and this client
polls `{url}/v1/database/{db}/sql` within `readyTimeoutMs`. When the pool has
no free database (exhausted or recycling, HTTP 503 with Retry-After), reset
retries within `leaseTimeoutMs`, then throws `PoolExhaustedError`.

`wipedModule` (bytes, or an async function returning them) makes
`reset("wiped")` upload that wasm to `POST /pool/lease-module` instead of
leasing from the pool's stored module: a branch that changes `server/` gets
a fresh database running its own build. The pool only ever creates a new
database for it; the upload is size-capped (413) and a module spacetime
rejects fails the reset (422) without leaving a lease.

Extras outside `WorldSource`: `release()` ends the current lease at the end
of a run; `mintCaller()` mints a second, non-owner identity on the same host
(`POST {url}/v1/identity`) for role-scoped callers.

Dependency-free on purpose: only `fetch`, which tests inject.

### [`src/docs/config.ts`](src/docs/config.ts)

What a package tells the generators about itself, in
`behaviour/docs.config.ts`. Everything else is read from the package: its
features, test results, header comments, unit-test markers and scripts.

### [`src/docs/sources.ts`](src/docs/sources.ts)

What the generated documents are made of, read offline from one package:
its .feature files and their @code links, the header comments of its source
files, and the annotation above each unit test. The README generator, the
guide generator and the drift checks all read through here, so they agree
on what counts as a scenario, a code link or a reason to keep a test.

### [`src/docs/readme.ts`](src/docs/readme.ts)

Render a package's README.md offline, in about a second, from what the
package is:

  behaviour/docs.config.ts  the commands (from the package's own schema or
                            usage text) and which files carry the design
  behaviour/**/*.feature    what the package promises, tested from outside
  docs/guide.md             the header line of the last behaviour run
  source header comments    the design: why each part is the way it is
  unit-test annotations     which unit tests stay, and why
  package.json              how to run the tests

Nothing in the README is written by hand. To change a sentence, change its
source; the package's docs drift test fails when the README differs.
The kept inventory has no shared total: independent row additions can merge
without leaving a stale count (proved in readme.test.ts).

### [`src/docs/guide.ts`](src/docs/guide.ts)

Project one behaviour run (allure-vitest results) into two documents:

  docs/guide.md      short and intent-first, for people and coding agents:
                     run header, the tested I/O contract, the commands, task
                     recipes, how to check the result yourself, known limits
  docs/scenarios.md  the evidence: every scenario with its real transcripts

Every sentence comes from a .feature file, the package's own command source
or its docs configuration; every example comes from a real run. Declared
constraints are labelled separately from execution evidence. A scenario
that did not pass is labelled, never shown as working. Setup runs
(the "Given" preparation) are hidden, and tool output that is left out is
counted, not silently dropped. A code link whose file or symbol does not
exist fails the generator. Both documents carry the hash of the .feature
files they come from, so a drift check can tell when they are stale.

### [`src/docs/checks.ts`](src/docs/checks.ts)

The drift checks a package's docs test runs offline: each returns what is
wrong, empty when the documents match their sources.

### [`src/docs/report.ts`](src/docs/report.ts)

The Allure 3 HTML report of the last behaviour run, for people who want to
click through scenarios, steps and transcripts. The results are the same
files the guide is generated from; nothing is re-run. The report is a
local, disposable view (behaviour/<scope>/.report, gitignored); the guide
and the evidence stay the committed documents.

### [`src/docs/main.ts`](src/docs/main.ts)

`behaviour-docs readme|guide [<package dir>]`: write a package's README.md
(offline) or its docs/guide.md and docs/scenarios.md (from the last run's
results in behaviour/.results) and the README that quotes the guide. The
package dir defaults to the cwd, which
is what `pnpm --filter <pkg> readme` gives.

## Behaviour suite

## Unit tests

A unit test stays only for what the behaviour suite cannot reach. The line above each test says why (`// keep(K…): …`, or one `// keep-file(K…): …` line for a whole file), or names the scenario it still lacks (`// open: …`).

- **K1** one of several cases over a pure function
- **K2** a branch the public surface cannot provoke without an injected host, process, fault or TTY
- **K3** a cross-run invariant (determinism, idempotence, ordering)
- **K4** a compile proof, snapshot or documentation drift gate
- **K5** a contract with another tool the suite does not drive (shell scripts, shared file formats)

**Kept**

| Test | File | Why it stays |
|---|---|---|
| all 2 tests in the file | [`cli.test.ts`](src/cli.test.ts) | K2: a tool that cannot start or never exits is an injected fault no suite meets on purpose. |
| README.md is what behaviour-docs readme writes | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: README drift gate |
| published docs name the checkout <repo>, also when a transcript already shortened home to ~ | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: generated docs must not leak the checkout path after transcripts shortened home to ~ |
| shows author-declared constraints even when every scenario passed | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: generated guide contract separates author declarations from executed evidence |
| renders the existing all-pass guide identically for absent and empty known limits | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: optional configuration must preserve existing generated documents byte for byte |
| keeps long JSON and cursor commands intact while truncating long output lines | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: published transcripts retain executable commands while bounding ordinary output |
| preserves quoted and continued command lines before filtering noise, ANSI or long output | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: a multiline command's literal data must survive every transcript cleanup stage |
| bounds ordinary output after an unmatched apostrophe in the recorded command | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: unmatched raw argv punctuation must not disable output cleanup or cross attachment boundaries |
| preserves historical applyset, doors and sk-dev rendering without claiming a new live run | [`docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) | K4: synthetic renderer fixtures pin six document outputs from the pre-change renderer |
| accepts two branches adding independent kept rows and rejects missing or changed rows | [`readme.test.ts`](src/docs/readme.test.ts) | K4: merged generated inventories must pass the consumer's drift gate while stale rows still fail |
| all 4 tests in the file | [`refusal.test.ts`](src/docs/refusal.test.ts) | K1: rule cases of one pure function over a transcript |
| reads a test's own marker, a file-wide marker, and reports a test with neither | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: marker grammar — a test's own line wins, a file line covers the rest |
| names an it.each case by its describe | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: marker grammar — an it.each title is named by its describe |
| turns a header comment into Markdown | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: comment grammar — line comments, block comments, links and lead-ins |
| checks @spec tags against the spec's scenario IDs, both ways | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: spec ID grammar — the heading form, and every tag on either side |
| reads one suite of several when a scope is given | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: scope rule — a suite's subfolder alone, for features, hash and spec tags |
| links a @code tag without a symbol to its file, labelled by the file name | [`sources.test.ts`](src/docs/sources.test.ts) | K1: code-tag grammar — a tag without a symbol names the file |
| holds independent reset endpoints until stop, with transport failures instead of HTTP answers | [`endpoint.test.ts`](src/endpoint.test.ts) | K2: real OS socket ownership and child lifetime cannot be proved by HTTP response assertions. |
| rejects an early exit with the child's log and exit status | [`endpoint.test.ts`](src/endpoint.test.ts) | K2: fail a real child before readiness and preserve its diagnostics for the test author. |
| rejects a spawn failure | [`endpoint.test.ts`](src/endpoint.test.ts) | K2: a missing executable must reject and clean up rather than leave a hanging startup promise. |
| stops a child that never reports readiness | [`endpoint.test.ts`](src/endpoint.test.ts) | K2: startup timeout must kill a listener that has not announced readiness. |
| all 6 tests in the file | [`world-pooled.test.ts`](src/world-pooled.test.ts) | K2: retry, readiness and error paths need an injected pool that refuses, delays or breaks |

**Open (0)**: reachable from outside; each goes once a scenario covers it.

None.

## Run

```bash
pnpm --filter @spellkave/behaviour test    # vitest run
pnpm --filter @spellkave/behaviour readme  # tsx src/docs/main.ts readme
```
